BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.claim: Al-Irshad reads this as unbelievers whose deeds were good in themselves, such as charity and freeing slaves, and who proudly expected reward from them.
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : هذا بيان حال الكفرة باعتبار ما صدر عنهم

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r4.claim: Their efforts to establish intrinsically good works are entirely wasted; the loss of their effort is not limited to worldly life.
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r4.anchor: في إقامة الأعمال الحسنة في أنفسها أي : ضاع وبطل بالكلية

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r5.claim: They imagine their efforts will benefit them in the afterlife because they admire the works they struggled to perform and think they did them properly.
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r5.anchor: يعني : يعملون عملا ينفعهم في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r6.claim: The inward warning includes innovators, people seeking reputation, and the ostentatious: even slight ostentation is hidden shirk that cancels deeds.
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى أهل الأهواء والبدع وأهل الرياء والسمعة فإن اليسير من الرياء شرك

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r7.claim: Deeds alongside disbelief or hidden association are rejected; this also warns against people seeking thanks from others and monks who impose harsh retreats while imagining they worship rightly.
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r7.anchor: وإذا كان ما هو طاعة مردودا لمجاورته المنافي فما ظنك بما هو معصية في نفسه

QIRAAT-ER:18:104:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:104:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:104:9#1/r1.claim: Kasra on sīn is a canonical dialectal variant; grammarians associate yaḥsabu with Hijazi and yaḥsibu with Tamimi.
QIRAAT-ER:18:104:9#1/r1.anchor: Some grammarians associate yaḥsabu with Ḥijāzī dialect and yaḥsibu with Tamīmī

SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.claim: People ruin their good works by reproaching recipients and demanding thanks, and ruin worship by performing it for show and reputation.
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : حين سئل عن هذه الآية قال : هو الذي يبطل معروفه في الدنيا مع أهلها بالمنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r5.claim: Ḍalla saʿyuhum means their effort perished, became void, and vanished. Yaḥsabūn and yuḥsinūn differ only by dots, an example of tajnīs al-taṣḥīf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r5.anchor: ضل سعيهم أي هلك وبطل وذهب ويحسبون ويحسنون من تجنيس التصحيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r6.speaker: البحتري، شاعر مجهول
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r6.claim: Al-Buhturi's line illustrates the dot-based wordplay; another poem is given in a deliberately mispointed form, then restored as “you watered me, my Lord …,” for the same unusual pun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r6.anchor: ومنه قول أبي عبادة البحتري: ولم يكن المغتر بالله إذ سرى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r1.claim: Their effort is wholly lost and void before God; “in worldly life” modifies their striving, since its failure is not limited to this world.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r1.anchor: أي ضاع وبطل بالكلية عند الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r2.claim: One transmitted interpretation identifies the people as Jews and Christians; their deeds include acts of worship whose rules were abrogated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r3.claim: Other identifications are monks who impose harsh ascetic exercises on themselves, and the Sabians.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r3.anchor: وقيل : الرهبان الذين يحسبون أنفسهم في الصوامع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r4.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r4.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwa asked about them, ʿAli reportedly said they were the Haruriyya, the Kharijites.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r4.anchor: عليا كرم الله تعالى وجهه عنهم فقال : منهم أهل حروراء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.claim: An objection says the next verse calls them unbelievers, unlike Kharijites who do not deny resurrection; the answer is that مِن can mean sharing only their misguidance, or ʿAli may have judged them unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.anchor: وأجيب بأن من اتصالية فلا يلزم أن يكونوا متصلين بهم من كل الوجوه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r6.claim: The author favors reading ʿAli’s attribution as a harsh allusion rather than a precise identification of the verse’s subjects.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r6.anchor: واستحسن أنه تعريض بهم على سبيل التغليظ لا تفسير للآية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r7.speaker: العياشي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r7.claim: A report cited by al-ʿAyyashi says ʿAli identified them as People of the Book who disbelieved in God and innovated in religion; it adds that the river people are not far from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r7.anchor: أولئك أهل الكتاب كفروا بربهم وابتدعوا في دينهم فحبطت أعمالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r8.claim: This report supports the earlier reconciliation and indicates that the description extends broadly to unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r8.anchor: وهذا يؤيد الجواب الأول وأخبر أن المراد ما يعمم سائر الكفرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r9.claim: The relative clause may answer an implied “who are they?”, explain الأخسرين, describe or substitute for it, or be an accusative rebuke; the last analysis fits poorly because its opening does not state the key loss.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r9.anchor: ومحل الموصول الرفع على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف لأنه جواب للسؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r10.claim: Doing a deed حسنًا means performing it suitably; they believe they work properly because they admire and invested effort in their acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r10.anchor: الاحسان الإتيان بالأعمال على الوجه اللائق وهو حسنها الوصفي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r11.claim: The circumstantial clause may modify the subject of “went astray” or their “striving”; the first makes their misguidance coincide with their mistaken belief and better exposes their error.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r11.anchor: والفرق بين الوجهين أن المقارن لحال حسبانهم المذكور في الأول ضلال سعيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r12.claim: The similar forms يحسبون and يحسنون produce a pun-like transposition of letters.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r12.anchor: قيل والأول أدخل في بيان خطئهم ولا يخفى ما بين يحسبون ويحسنون من تجنيس التصحيف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r13.speaker: البحتري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r13.claim: Al-Buhturi’s line about the one who trusts in God and the one who seeks Him illustrates the sound-play.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r13.anchor: قول البحتري : ولم يكن المغتر بالله إذ سرى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.claim: They identify the losers as Jews and Christians.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص: هم اليهود والنصارى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.claim: Another view identifies them as monks who confined themselves to monasteries.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: هم الرهبان. {الذين} حبسوا أنفسهم في الصوامع.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.claim: He identifies them as the people of Ḥarūrāʾ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: هم أهل حروراء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.claim: Their effort was null and void in worldly life, although they thought their work was good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.anchor: {ضل سعيهم} بطل عملهم واجتهادهم {في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا}

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r1.claim: Their efforts are wasted through disbelief and self-admiration, like monks who lose both worldly life and the next; the clause can be parsed as predicate, apposition, or blame.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r1.anchor: ضاع وبطل لكفرهم وعجبهم كالرهابنة فإنهم خسروا دنياهم وأخراهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r2.claim: They imagine their work is good because of vanity and conviction that they are right.

NAHHAS:v2p475/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p475/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p475/r8.claim: ‘Those whose effort was lost’ can modify ‘the greatest losers’ in the genitive, or be a nominative meaning ‘they,’ or an accusative meaning ‘I mean.’
NAHHAS:v2p475/r8.anchor: في موضع خفض على النعت للأخسرين ، ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع بمعنى هم ، ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب بمعنى أعني

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r3.claim: Their effort went astray because they turned from the only one who can benefit or harm them toward things that do neither.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r3.anchor: الإعراض عمن لا ينفعهم ولا يضرهم إلا هو

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r4.claim: Despite the obvious failure, they imagine their work is expertly done because their judgment is weak.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r4.anchor: أي فعلا هو في غاية الإحكام

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.claim: Ka'b says the Quran appears as a beautiful, fragrant companion to the person who acted by it, soothes his terror, and identifies itself as his good deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.anchor: عن كعب قال: يمثل القرآن لمن كان يعمل به في الدنيا يوم القيامة كأحسن صورة رآها وجها أحسنه وأطيبه ريحا

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.claim: The Quran asks God to intercede for its companion, reminding Him that it occupied his days with thirst and nights with wakefulness; he is then crowned and robed in honor.
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.anchor: طالما اظمأت نهاره وأسهرت ليله فشفعني فيه فيوضع تاج الملك على رأسه ويكسى حلة الملك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.claim: The passage answers those who worship useless idols as patrons and seek their favor, making their work and effort futile; the key rebuke is that they think they do well.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.anchor: فإنهم لما اتخذوا أولياء من ليسوا ينفعونهم فاختاروا الأصنام وعبدوها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r1.claim: Those whose effort went astray is an appositive to the losers, extending the description to heighten suspense about their identity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r1.anchor: وقوله { الذين ضل سعيهم } بدل من { بالأخسرين أعمالا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r2.claim: Ḍalāl means missing the path; unfruitful effort is likened to travel along a road that leads nowhere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r2.anchor: والضلال : خطأ السبيل . شبه سعيهم غير المثمر بالسير في طريق غير موصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r3.claim: Saʿy literally means vigorous walking and is metaphorical for work, as in 17:19; they worshiped idols believing their acts would fulfill their aims and count as good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r3.anchor: والسعي : المشي في شدة . وهو هنا مجاز في العمل كما تقدم عند قوله { ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r4.claim: Attributing error to the effort is a figurative attribution: the people themselves went astray in their efforts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r4.anchor: وإسناد الضلال إلى سعيهم مجاز عقلي . والمعنى : الذين ضلوا في سعيهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r5.claim: Yaḥsabūn and yuḥsinūn form a paronomasia distinguished by dot placement, an example in the rhetoric manuals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r5.anchor: وبين يحسبون } و { يحسنون } جناس مصحف ، وقد مثل بهما في مبحث الجناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.claim: The question about the greatest losers is a taunting rebuke addressed to the disbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.anchor: ثم قال تعالى: هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا الآية المعنى: قل لهؤلاء الكفرة على جهة التوبيخ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r1.claim: Their effort and work in worldly life came to nothing even while they believed they were doing good.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r1.anchor: الذين ضل سعيهم أي بطل عملهم واجتهادهم في الدنيا وهم يظنون أنهم محسنون بأفعالهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r2.claim: Their leaders know what is correct but choose falsehood to preserve their status; their followers imitate them without evidence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r2.anchor: فرؤساؤهم يعلمون الصحيح ويؤثرون الباطل لبقاء رئاستهم وأتباعهم مقلدون بغير دليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.claim: Asked whether the greatest losers are the Haruriyya, Sa'd answers that they are Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, while Christians denied food and drink in Paradise; the Haruriyya break God's covenant after pledging it, and Sa'd called them profligates. Bukhari transmits this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.anchor: سألت أبي -يعني سعد بن أبي وقاص-: {قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا} أهم الحرورية؟ قال: لا هم اليهود والنصارى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.claim: Ali, al-Dahhak, and others identify the greatest losers as the Haruriyya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب (1) والضحاك، وغير واحد: هم الحرورية.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.claim: The verse broadly includes the Haruriyya alongside Jews, Christians, and others; it is not exclusive to any group, since it is Meccan, before the relevant Jewish-Christian address and before the Khawarij existed. It covers anyone who follows an unapproved way while thinking the work is accepted, as echoed in 88:2–4, 25:23, and 24:39.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.anchor: أن هذه الآية الكريمة تشمل الحرورية كما تشمل اليهود والنصارى وغيرهم، لا أنها نزلت في هؤلاء على الخصوص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.claim: The greatest losers are those whose efforts were invalid under a lawful, pleasing religious way, yet who believe they are doing well and that their deeds are accepted and loved.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.anchor: أي: عملوا أعمالا باطلة على غير شريعة مشروعة مرضية مقبولة

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r1.claim: Hisban and zann are near synonyms; liqaʾ means nearness without separation, and meeting and contact are related terms; mockery and derision are synonyms.
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r1.anchor: والحسبان والظن من النظائر. واللقاء: قرب الشيء من الشيء من غير فصل

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.claim: Those who assume worship of others benefits them are the greatest losers: they exhaust themselves in deeds they think right, then end in the Fire.
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.anchor: أكثر خسرانا على تحملهم لأنهم أتعبوا أنفسهم في أعمالهم ظنا أنهم على شيء

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r14.claim: One sense of their lost effort is that they tried to destroy religion but failed to attain their aim.
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r14.anchor: أحدهما: سعيهم في الكفر وإبطال الدين، فلم يحصل مرادهم وبطل سعيهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r1.claim: الذين ضل may be genitive as adjective, appositive, or explanatory substitute; accusative for censure; or nominative as predicate of an omitted topic.
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r1.anchor: يجوز فيه الجر نعتا وبدلا وبيانا،

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r2.claim: The closeness of يحسبون and يحسنون is a strong example of orthographic wordplay, called تجنيس التصحيف or تجنيس الخط.

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r3.speaker: البحتري
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r3.claim: Al-Buhturi's verse contrasts المغتر بالله from غرور with المعتز بالله from عز, illustrating the wordplay.
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r3.anchor: ولم يكن المغتر بالله إذ شرى

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r4.speaker: شاعر مجهول
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r4.claim: A cited poem's wording is then deliberately misread into a different sequence of near-identical written words to show the device.
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r4.anchor:
سقينني ريي وغنينني
يحت بحبي حين بن الخرد

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r5.speaker: رسائل الفصحاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r5.claim: An eloquent-letter example strings together similar written forms in قبل قبل يدك ثراك and عبد عند رخاك رجاك.
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r5.anchor: قبل قبل يدك ثراك، عبد عند رخاك رجاك،

MUQATIL:18:103-107/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r2.claim: Their effort is wasted, yet they think they are doing good.
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r2.anchor: { الذين ضل سعيهم } ، يعني حبطت أعمالهم التي عملوها، { في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا } [آية: 104].

NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#5/r1.claim: Their effort was wasted and void; the relative clause is nominative, meaning “they are those” whose effort went astray.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#5/r1.anchor: ضاع وبطل وهو في محل الرفع أي هم الذين

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as the disbelievers of Mecca.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد كفار أهل مكة

ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r2.claim: The people meant are disbelievers whose works do not benefit them; another verse says God frustrates the deeds of disbelievers.
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r2.anchor: كما قال تعالى: (الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله أضل أعمالهم)

ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r3.claim: الذين may be genitive as an adjective for الأخسرين or nominative as a new sentence; يحسبون has two readings.
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r3.anchor: و (الذين) يصلح أن يكون جرا ورفعأ، فالجر نعت للأخسرين.

STUDYQURAN:18:103/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r2.claim: They consider their work virtuous, as other verses say the deeds of disbelievers and wrongdoers seem fair to them.
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r2.anchor: Such people reckon that they are virtuous in their works, for as mentioned in several verses the deeds of the disbelievers and wrongdoers seem fair to them

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.claim: These six verses draw a conclusion from the sūrah’s account of worldly seduction, reliance on protectors besides God, spiritual blindness, and bad outcomes, and prepare for the closing declaration at 18:110.
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.anchor: بيان الآيات الست في منزلة الاستنتاج مما تقدم من آيات السورة

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r3.claim: A person may lose in an undertaking because the effort misses its goal, like a mistaken journey or lost capital; such a loss may be repaired if its cause is recognized.
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r3.anchor: إنما يتحقق إذا لم يصب الكسب والسعي غرضه وانتهى إلى نقص في رأس المال

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r4.claim: The worst loss is to suffer while believing one profits: unlike an acknowledged mistake, it offers no hope of correction because the person does not see the failure.
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r4.anchor: لا يرى غير ذلك وهو أشد الخسران

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r5.claim: Those who settle in falsehood and mistake it for good are the most hopelessly lost: worldly desires, arrogance, and inherited zeal veil the truth and block its call.
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r5.anchor: من جهة انجذاب نفوسهم إلى زينات الدنيا وزخارفها وانغمارهم في الشهوات

TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.claim: The greatest losers in works are disbelieving Jews and Christians whose efforts in worldly life came to nothing while they thought their actions were virtuous acts of obedience and worship.
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.anchor: وهم كفار أهل الكتاب اليهود والنصارى

TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.speaker: العياشي
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about the greatest losers: Ali identified scriptural communities who disbelieved and innovated, adding that the Khawarij were not far from them.
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.anchor: أولئك أهل الكتاب كفروا بربهم وابتدعوا في دينهم

THALABI:v6p200#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p200#2/r4.claim: They are people whose worldly effort went astray while they thought they were obedient and doing good.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r4.anchor: أي يظنون أنهم بفعلهم مطيعون محسنون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r1.claim: “Those whose striving went astray” can be genitive as an adjective of “the greatest losers,” or nominative as a fresh sentence meaning “they are those.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r1.anchor: يجوز في {الذين} الخفض بالنعت للأخسرين. ويجوز الرفع على الاستيئناف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r2.claim: Their effort and work in worldly life were fruitless, though they believed they were doing well.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r3.claim: “Sunʿ” is the verbal noun of doing a favor and is most often used for good works.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r3.anchor: والصنع: مصدر صنع إليه معروفا يصنع صنعا، وأكثر ما يستعمل الصنع في الأعمال الحسنة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r5.claim: Their effort is void in worldly life even though they imagine their deeds are obedient and virtuous.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says the people's effort goes astray, though they think they are doing well; Yaḥyā identifies them as the People of the Book.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.anchor: {بالأخسرين أعمالا {103} الذين ضل سعيهم} [الكهف: 103-104] يعني: يضل سعيهم. وهو تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r2.speaker: علي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r2.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwāʾ asked ʿAlī who the verse describes, ʿAlī answered: the people of Ḥarūrāʾ.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r2.anchor: وحدثني المعلى، عن عمار الدهني، عن أبي الطفيل أن ابن الكواء سأل عليا عنها قال: ويلك منهم أهل حروراء.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.claim: People direct their efforts toward their aims: seeking God’s pleasure and the afterlife leads to one kind of work, while pursuit of worldly gain leads to another.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.anchor: İnsanlar, davranışlarında daima bir amaç gözetip ona göre çaba harcarlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.claim: Polytheists think their idols bring them nearer to God and that shirk is obedience, but God gives their deeds no value in this life or the next.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.anchor: Allah’a ortak koşanlar tanrılarının kendilerini Allah’a yaklaştıracağını ve Allah katında küfür sayılan bu davranışlarının Allah’a itaat olduğunu sanmaktadırlar.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: These verses humble people who thought themselves superior and mocked revelation: they will become insignificant and taste Hell as the consequence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Today they regard themselves to be superior but on the Day of Judgement they will become insignificant. They haughtily made fun of God’s revelations

QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:105/r1.claim: In the preceding wording, أعمالا is accusative as a specification (tamyīz).

TABATABAI:18:105-107/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r1.claim: The preceding description means they inwardly know truth but persist in rejecting it from arrogance, desire, and self-satisfaction, as in the cited examples.
TABATABAI:18:105-107/r1.anchor: فاتباعهم هوى أنفسهم ومضيهم على ما هم عليه من الإعراض عن الحق عنادا واستكبارا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p56/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p56/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p56/r3.claim: The verse about people who lose their worldly efforts while thinking they do good points to ostentatious people, including lodge-dwellers who court attention and ensnare the wealthy; they are exposed here and face expulsion and painful punishment in the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p56/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى : ( الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا ) إشارة إلى المرائين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p56/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p56/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p56/r4.claim: Alusi specifically includes those who sit in a lodge to attract public notice and ensnare worldly people through schemes.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p56/r4.anchor: ومنهم الذين يجلسون في الخانقاه لأجل نظر الخلق وصرف وجوه الناس إليهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r10.claim: The losers' efforts are wasted because they worked for other than God, so their deeds do not benefit them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r10.anchor: ضل سعيهم لأنهم عملوا لغير الله . وما كان لغير الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r11.claim: Another account identifies them as people who mix deeds with ostentation and self-admiration, undoing good through self-regard or reminding others of favors.
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r11.anchor: الذين قرنوا أعمالهم بالرياء ، ووصفوا أحوالهم بالإعجاب

QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r12.claim: A further account describes people who scrutinize their deeds and regard them with self-importance rather than seeing them as small.
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r12.anchor: هم الذين يلاحظون أعمالهم وما منهم بعين الاستكثار

QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r13.claim: They lack spiritual verification and act without knowledge or certainty, blinded to truth and left in delusions, with no weight in the next life.
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r13.anchor: لم يكونوا أصحاب التحقيق ، فعملوا من غير علم

QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r14.claim: Their condition reverses across time: present denial and separation become future rejection and burning, while the elect have immediate gardens of union and future gardens of grace.
QUSHAYRI:v2p230/r14.anchor: اليوم هم في ذل الفراق ، وغدا في أليم الاحتراق

JISHUMI:v6p4506/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4506/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4506/r4.claim: A person may be sinful through an act without realizing that it is sinful.
JISHUMI:v6p4506/r4.anchor: وتدل أنه قد يكون عاصيا بفعل لا يعلم أنه معصية

MAJAZ:v1p416/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p416/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p416/r2.claim: صنعا means work and is equivalent to الصنعة and الصنيع; a صنيع horse is made or fashioned.
MAJAZ:v1p416/r2.anchor: «يحسنون صنعا» (104) أي عملا والصنع والصنعة والصنيع واحد

TABATABAI:18:108/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:18:108/r3.claim: In response to Ibn al-Kawwa’s question about the greatest losers, Ali identifies them as the sinful people of Quraysh.
TABATABAI:18:108/r3.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل قال سمعت علي بن أبي طالب وسأله ابن الكوا فقال

TABATABAI:18:108/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:18:108/r4.claim: A report through al-Ayyashi says the losers are People of the Book who disbelieved and innovated; it adds that the people of the River are not far from them.
TABATABAI:18:108/r4.anchor: قام ابن الكوا إلى أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام فقال أخبرني عن قول الله

TABATABAI:18:108/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:108/r5.claim: The author notes another report identifying the losers as Christians.
TABATABAI:18:108/r5.anchor: أقول وروي أنهم النصاري، القمي عن أبي جعفر

TABATABAI:18:108/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:18:108/r6.claim: Al-Qummi and al-Tabarsi transmit that the losers are People of the Book.
TABATABAI:18:108/r6.anchor: القمي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام والطبرسي في الاحتجاج عن علي عليه السلام أنهم أهل الكتاب

TABATABAI:18:108/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:18:108/r7.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim identifies them as monks who secluded themselves in pillars.
TABATABAI:18:108/r7.anchor: عن أبي خميصة عبد الله بن قيس عن علي عليه السلام أنهم الرهبان الذين حبسوا أنفسهم في السواري

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r1.claim: Sa'y means running or brisk walking; ihsan is mastery rather than ordinary work. Fi'l can describe an inanimate thing, 'amal need not be skilled making, and sun' is finer, intentional work by a rational agent.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r1.anchor: والإحسان هو الإتقان وليس العمل العادي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r2.claim: The verse combines misguidance, striving, and skilled making, so it fittingly says “greatest losers in deeds”; it is the Qur'an's only attribution of loss to work, in a passage framed throughout by deeds.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r2.anchor: جاء فيها ضلال وسعي وصُنع لذا استوجب أن يؤتى بكلمة الأخسرين أعمالاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r3.claim: Al-akhsarin is a comparative superlative: many are losers, and some are worse than others, so the ranking is among the losers themselves.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r3.anchor: الأخسرين: اسم تفضيل أي أنه هناك اشتراك في الخُسران، يوجد خاسرون كُثُر والأخسرين بعضهم أخسر من بعض

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةوهوبابالنسبة)#556.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةوهوبابالنسبة)#556.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةوهوبابالنسبة)#556.claim: On nisba formation, al-Khalīl says forms the Arabs reshaped outside the regular pattern remain in that reshaped form, while forms left complete follow analogy.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةوهوبابالنسبة)#556.anchor: قال الخليل كل شيء من ذلك عدلته

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p31/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p31/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p31/r1.claim: Saad Zaghlul praised al-Rafi‘i’s book and Yaqub Sarruf urged Muslims who owned a Quran to own it too, though Bint al-Shati says neither was an authority on the subject.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p31/r1.anchor: كما قال الدكتور يعقوب صروف فى تقريظه للكتاب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p31/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p31/r2.speaker: مصطفى صادق الرافعي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p31/r2.claim: In his third-edition preface, al-Rafi‘i denounces critics as people who disguise ignorance as science and act from malice, imitation, and corrupt character.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p31/r2.anchor: فيقف الرافعى منهم مثل الموقف الذى أنكره على السلف

NASHR:v2p82/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r1.claim: A feminine ending written tāʾ is pronounced hāʾ at pause, and some Arabs imala it like alif.
NASHR:v2p82/r1.anchor: وهي الهاء التي تكون في الوصل تاء آخر الاسم نحو: نعمة ورحمة فتبدل في الوقف هاء

NASHR:v2p82/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r2.speaker: الكسائي
NASHR:v2p82/r2.claim: When asked why he imala before feminine hāʾ, al-Kisai said this is Arabic’s natural way.
NASHR:v2p82/r2.anchor: وقيل للكسائي إنك تميل ما قبل هاء التأنيث فقال: هذا طباع العربية

NASHR:v2p82/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p82/r3.claim: Al-Dani identifies this imala as a Kufan dialect that remained among their descendants; al-Akhfash also reports the usage.
NASHR:v2p82/r3.anchor: قال الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني يعني بذلك أن الإمالة هنا لغة أهل الكوفة، وهي باقية فيهم إلى الآن

NASHR:v2p82/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r4.claim: The author says this imala remains widespread and easier on speakers’ tongues; Sibawayh explains it by treating hāʾ like alif.
NASHR:v2p82/r4.anchor: شبه الهاء بالألف فأمال ما قبلها كما يميل ما قبل الألف

NASHR:v2p82/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r5.claim: Al-Kisai has agreed, condition-governed cases of imala before feminine endings; other readers also agree in some cases.
NASHR:v2p82/r5.anchor: وقد اختص بإمالتها الكسائي في حروف مخصوصة بشروط معروفة باتفاق واختلاف

NASHR:v2p82/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r6.claim: The first agreed category covers fifteen consonants, summarized by the mnemonic فَجَثَت زينب لذود شمس.
NASHR:v2p82/r6.anchor: فالقسم الأول المتفق على إمالته قبل هاء التأنيث وما أشبهها خمسة عشر حرفا يجمعها قولك

NASHR:v2p82/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r7.claim: The fāʾ case occurs in twenty-one nouns, including khalīfa, raʾfa, al-khaṭfa, and khīfa.
NASHR:v2p82/r7.anchor: ورد في أحد وعشرين اسما نحو خليفة، رأفة، الخطفة، خيفة

NASHR:v2p82/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r8.claim: The jīm case occurs in eight nouns, including walīja, ḥāja, bahja, luja, naʿja, ḥajja, daraja, and zujāja.
NASHR:v2p82/r8.anchor: في ثمانية أسماء، وهي وليجة، حاجة، بهجة، لجة، نعجة، حجة، درجة، زجاجة

NASHR:v2p82/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r9.claim: The thāʾ case occurs in four nouns: thalātha, wāritha, khabītha, and mabthūtha.
NASHR:v2p82/r9.anchor: في أربعة أسماء، وهي ثلاثة، ورثة، خبيثة، مبثوثة

NASHR:v2p82/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r10.claim: The tāʾ case occurs in four nouns: al-mayta, baghta, al-mawta, and sitta.
NASHR:v2p82/r10.anchor: في أربعة أسماء أيضا الميتة، بغتة، الموتة، ستة

NASHR:v2p82/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r11.claim: The zāy case occurs in six nouns, including al-ʿizza, bāriza, bimafāza, hamza, and lamza.
NASHR:v2p82/r11.anchor: في ستة أسماء أعز، العزة، بارزة، بمفازة، همزة، لمزة

NASHR:v2p82/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r12.claim: The yāʾ case appears in sixty-four nouns, including shiya, diya, ḥaya, khashya, and zāniya.
NASHR:v2p82/r12.anchor: وردت في أربعة وستين اسما نحو شية، دية، حية، خشية، زانية

NASHR:v2p82/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r13.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r13.claim: The nūn case occurs in thirty-seven nouns, with examples including sana, al-janna, laʿna, and zaytūna.
NASHR:v2p82/r13.anchor: في سبعة وثلاثين اسما نحو: سنة، سنة، الجنة، الجنة، لعنة، زيتونة

NASHR:v2p82/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r14.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r14.claim: The bāʾ case occurs in twenty-eight nouns, including ḥabba, al-tawba, al-kaʿba, and Ghayāba.
NASHR:v2p82/r14.anchor: في ثمانية وعشرين اسما نحو حبة، التوبة، الكعبة، وشيبة، الإربة، غيابة

NASHR:v2p82/r15.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r15.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r15.claim: The lām case occurs in forty-five nouns, including layla, ghafla, ʿayla, al-nakhla, thulla, and al-ḍalāla.
NASHR:v2p82/r15.anchor: في خمسة وأربعين اسما نحو ليلة، غفلة، عيلة، النخلة، ثلة، الضلالة

NASHR:v2p82/r16.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r16.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r16.claim: The dhāl case occurs in two nouns: ladhdha and al-mawqūdha.

NASHR:v2p82/r17.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r17.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r17.claim: The wāw case occurs in seventeen nouns, including قسوة, المروة, نجوى, and أسوة.
NASHR:v2p82/r17.anchor: في سبعة عشر اسما نحو: قسوة، والمروة، نجوى، أسوة

NASHR:v2p82/r18.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r18.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r18.claim: The dāl case occurs in twenty-eight nouns, including balda, jilda, ʿidda, qirada, and afʾida.
NASHR:v2p82/r18.anchor: في ثمانية وعشرين اسما نحو: بلدة، جلدة، عدة، قردة، أفئدة

NASHR:v2p82/r19.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r19.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r19.claim: The shīn case occurs in four nouns: al-baṭsha, fāḥisha, ʿaysha, and maʿīsha.
NASHR:v2p82/r19.anchor: في أربعة أسماء البطشة فاحشة، عيشة، معيشة

NASHR:v2p82/r20.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r20.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r20.claim: The mīm case occurs in thirty-two nouns, including raḥma, niʿma, umma, qāʾima, and al-ṭāmma.
NASHR:v2p82/r20.anchor: في اثنين وثلاثين اسما نحو رحمة، نعمة، أمة، قائمة، الطامة

NASHR:v2p82/r21.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p82/r21.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p82/r21.claim: The sīn case occurs in three nouns: khamsa, al-khāmisa, and al-muqaddasa.
NASHR:v2p82/r21.anchor: في ثلاثة أسماء، وهي خمسة، والخامسة، المقدسة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r1.claim: Unlike rare, boastful public performances remembered for a clever or rhymed turn, the Qur’an offers a fresh literary style spanning dialogue, preaching, argument, maxims, stories, description, and narration for every kind of mind and purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r1.anchor: فجاء القرآن بأسلوب في الأدب غض جديد صالح لكل العقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r2.claim: Eloquent diction, fitting structure, and novel sound-patterned endings make the Qur’an memorable and quick to spread among tribes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r2.anchor: كان لذلك سريع العلوق بالحوافظ خفيف الانتقال والسير في القبائل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r3.claim: The Qur’an’s substance is truth rather than fabricated boast, giving it the force of truth and an effect Ibn ʿĀshūr calls spiritual rather than verbal or semantic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r3.anchor: مع كون مادته ولحمته هي الحقيقة دون المبالغات الكاذبة والمفاخرات المزعومة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r4.claim: The Qur’an uses rhetorical ornament more often than Arabic poetry, especially paronomasia; Ibn ʿĀshūr cites this verse as an example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r4.anchor: وقد رأيت المحسنات في البديع جاءت في القرآن أكثر مما جاءت في شعر العرب ، وخاصة الجناس كقوله ) وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr illustrates antithesis with the wording about leading astray and guiding to the punishment of the Blaze.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r5.anchor: والطباق كقوله ) كتب عليه أنه من تولاه فأنه يضله ويهديه إلى عذاب السعير (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r6.claim: Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ wrote a book devoted to Qur’anic rhetorical ornament.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p119/r6.anchor: وقد ألف ابن أبي الإصبع كتابا في بديع القرآن

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r1.claim: Lexical metaphor transfers an individual word from its original language meaning to another through resemblance or an association, as with hand for blessing or lion for a man.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r1.anchor: وصفنا بالمجاز الكلمة المفردة كقولنا اليد مجاز في النعمة والأسد مجاز في الإنسان

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r2.claim: A sentence is rational metaphor when its predication is figurative: assigning an action to a subject depends on the speaker’s intent, not lexical convention.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r2.anchor: متى وصفنا بالمجاز الجملة من الكلام كان مجازا من طريق المعقول دون اللغة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r3.claim: Saying spring made or embroidered a line attributes agency to an inanimate thing; that is a rational trope, since language itself does not prohibit such predication.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r3.anchor: فإذا قلنا مثلا خط أحسن مما وشاة الربيع أو صنعه الربيع كنا قد ادعينا في ظاهر اللفظ أن للربيع فعلا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r4.claim: Language determines the verb’s action and tense, but the speaker determines who is asserted to perform it, whether the assertion is true or imagined.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r4.anchor: أن ضرب لإثبات الضرب وليس لإثبات الخروج وانه لإثباته في زمان ماض وليس لإثباته في زمان مستقبل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r5.claim: Words and written forms are conventional signs rather than rationally necessary pairings, as shown by the differing languages and scripts.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p355/r5.anchor: ولو كان كذلك لم تختلف المواضعات في الألفاظ والخطوط ولكانت اللغات واحدة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r9.speaker: علي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r9.claim: Ali counts the people of Ḥarūrāʾ among those whose efforts go astray while they think they do good.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r9.anchor: قال فمن ﴿ الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا ﴾ قال كانت أهل حروراء منهم

BURHAN:v3p448/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p448/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p448/r9.claim: Written paronomasia pairs words that resemble one another in script but differ in sound, as in “they suppose” and “they do well.”
BURHAN:v3p448/r9.anchor: وإما في الخط وهو أن تشتبها في الخط لا اللفظ كقوله تعالى ﴿ وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا ﴾

ITQAN:v3p244/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p244/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p244/r9.claim: The cited phrase combines dot-based and vowel-based alteration, joining taṣḥīf and taḥrīf.
ITQAN:v3p244/r9.anchor: وقد اجتمع التصحيف والتحريف في قوله ﴿ وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا ﴾
